issues.description: Docstring deprecation directive has a typo 'stlib' that should be 'stdlib'.
issues.detail: The .. deprecated:: 4.3 block reads 'Use the stlib's' — this lands in rendered docs and misnames the replacement API. Trivial fix worth landing in the same commit.

issues.description: Deprecation message should show the replacement for the both-streams case.
issues.detail: The warning names contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr but doesn't explain how to compose them when callers were redirecting both. A one-line note pointing to nested with-statements or ExitStack closes the loop and preserves the original postcondition for two-stream users.

issues.description: Deprecation test is thin — stderr path uncovered and warning match is loose.
issues.detail: The test only exercises the stdout redirect and matches on the 'Please use...' suffix of the warning. Add an stderr-redirect assertion to cover the full deprecated surface, and tighten the match to something stable like 'deprecated' or the function name so prefix rewording doesn't silently pass.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this PR as a clean, well-scoped deprecation: falcon.testing.redirected is replaced by stdlib contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr, which preserves the contract (streams restored on exit, including on exception). The diff is small, the news fragment and test are present, and substitutability holds. Consensus nits: fix the 'stlib' typo, extend the deprecation message to cover the both-streams composition, and strengthen the test to cover stderr and use a more stable warning match. ACCEPT with trivial fixups.
